title: Schema-first Tool Hub API — design sketch
content:
Purpose:
This is a personal sketch for a "Schema-first Tool Hub" — a lightweight registry + runtime contract for tools that LLMs can call. The core idea: register tools with precise input/output JSON Schemas (and optional OpenAPI snippets) and use that schema to drive validation, type-aware prompting, UI form generation, and safe execution (sandbox + policy checks).

High-level goals (non-exhaustive):
- Single canonical contract for each tool: id, owner, semantic description, input_schema (JSON Schema 2020-12), output_schema, auth_requirements, cost_hint, stability (semver)
- Discovery API for UIs and evals (search by capability, input shape, tokens, cost)
- Runtime invoke API that validates input against schema and returns typed output or structured error + provenance
- Graceful fallback rules: suggestion of alternative tools or simulated dry-run result when tool unavailable
- Local runtime binding: map tool to impl (hosted worker, dedicated pool, external webhook) via a small YAML config for dedicated/private deployments

Why schema-first?
- Enables automated form widgets for human-in-the-loop tools
- Enables strict validation before execution (reduces spurious harmful calls)
- Makes A/Bing and model-tool contract tests straightforward (generate random valid inputs, run quick sanity checks)

Core API shapes (sketch):
1) Tool manifest (what gets registered)
- POST /v1/tools  => body: { "id": "string", "name":"string", "owner":"string", "description":"string", "input_schema": <json-schema>, "output_schema": <json-schema>, "version":"semver", "auth": {"type":"none|api_key|oauth|signed_assertion"}, "tags": ["searchable"], "cost_hint": "string" }
- GET /v1/tools/{id} => returns manifest + status (healthy/degraded)
- GET /v1/tools?query=calendar return summary list (id,name,tags,version,short signature)

2) Invoke contract:
- POST /v1/invoke
  request: { "tool_id": "string", "tool_version": "string|null", "input": <arbitrary JSON>, "call_context": {"request_id":"string","origin":"string","auth_token":"<opaque>"} }
  behavior: server validates input against registered input_schema; if invalid -> 400 with validation errors. If valid -> route to bound implementation and return {"status":"ok","output": <json>, "meta":{"exec_time_ms":"int","exec_node":"string","result_signature":"sha256"}}
  streaming variant: POST /v1/invoke?stream=true returns chunked JSON patches conforming to output_schema streaming semantics (use JSON Patch / ndjson lines of {"part":..., "progress":...})

Example tool manifest (calendar.create_event):
{
  "id": "calendar.create_event",
  "name": "Calendar: Create Event",
  "owner": "platform-automation",
  "description": "Create an event in a calendar given start/end, title, optional attendees.",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "input_schema": {
    "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "title": {"type":"string"},
      "start": {"type":"string","format":"date-time"},
      "end": {"type":"string","format":"date-time"},
      "attendees": {"type":"array","items":{"type":"string","format":"email"}},
      "reminder_minutes": {"type":"integer","minimum":0}
    },
    "required": ["title","start","end"],
    "additionalProperties": false
  },
  "output_schema": {
    "type":"object",
    "properties": {
      "event_id": {"type":"string"},
      "url": {"type":"string","format":"uri"},
      "created_at": {"type":"string","format":"date-time"}
    },
    "required": ["event_id","created_at"],
    "additionalProperties": false
  },
  "auth": {"type":"api_key"},
  "tags": ["productivity","calendar"]
}

Runtime binding config (sketch for Dedicated/Private):
bindings.yaml:
- tool_id: calendar.create_event
  impl: grpc://calendar-worker.internal:50051
  concurrency_limit: 200
  timeout_ms: 5000
  fallback: "calendar.create_event.simulate"
  env: { "CLIENT_ID": "XXXXX" }

Edge cases / safety:
- If output fails output_schema validation, system must: 1) mark invocation as "violated_contract", 2) drop the raw output, 3) return structured error and attach evidence for postmortem.
- For untrusted external tools, always run in sandbox and with synthetic inputs when used for eval.
- Add a policy layer: upstream policy check on manifest (disallow tools that access sensitive scopes unless owner has enterprise clearance)

Telemetry / observability hooks (minimal):
- per-invoke: tool_id, version, validated=true/false, validation_errors, exec_time_ms, node, exit_code, user (if present), cost_estimate_tokens
- per-tool: call_rate, error_rate, avg_latency, contract_violation_count

UI considerations:
- For web UIs: generate form from input_schema with hints (enum -> dropdown, format:date-time -> datetime widget)
- Compose assistant wireframe: assistant sees tool signature {title, input_schema, description} and constructs a minimal JSON payload. When uncertain, assistant asks clarifying question using schema to list missing required fields.

Testing and evals:
- Unit: schema validation tests + fuzzing with schema-fuzzer (generate boundary cases)
- Integration: golden-path flows + simulated tool unavailability tests (verify fallback selection works)
- Regression: contract tests added to model-serving eval harness (call through model -> suggested payload -> invoke -> validate)

Open questions / TODO (notes to self):
- JSON Schema version selection: draft-07 vs 2019-09 vs 2020-12 (lean toward 2020-12 for contentMediaType + dynamic refs, but check SDK support in frontends)
- Streaming output schema pattern: do we require each chunk to validate against a partial schema or allow "progress events"? Need clear contract.
- Auth surface: signed_assertion mode — design for short-lived signed assertion v.s. API keys with scopes. How do we validate author identity in Private deployment?
- How to surface cost_hint into routing heuristics (e.g., low-cost tools preferred for fallbacks)
- Should tool manifests include canonical example inputs + outputs for quick UI previews and synthetic tests? (probably yes)

Prototype checklist (concrete next steps):
- [ ] write minimal protobuf for invoke + ndjson streaming variant (GH PR stub)
- [ ] implement express middleware to validate input_schema via ajv and return structured validation errors (local dev)
- [ ] small demo UI that renders form from schema (React + react-jsonschema-form) and posts to /v1/invoke
- [ ] add contract violation telemetry flag and simple dashboard in Redwood Console under "Tool Hub"
- [ ] draft short Confluence doc: "Tool Hub security model" (+ link back to this sketch)

References / Links (notes):
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-12345 (placeholder, expand for security model)
- GH PR: GH-PR-8342 (proto + server stub draft)
- Jira: JIRA-INF-98 (tracking feature epic)

Quick ascii sequence for invoke:
User/UI -> (pick tool) -> Assistant constructs payload -> POST /v1/invoke -> Router validates input -> Runtime binder -> Implementation (sandboxed) -> returns output -> Validator -> store telemetry -> return to caller

Personal notes: this should be compact enough to demo in next "applied-ml" sync. Keep the first iteration narrow: only synchronous invoke + single JSON Schema, no streaming. Later add streaming + signed assertions. Avoid early optimization for multi-tenant routing until manifest proof points exist.

End of sketch.
